label: r4c2
name: shared aligner, wider stem
hypothesis: Same as r3c3, but the per-cell 1x1 stem widens from 64 to 128 hidden units. Stacking correctly means comparing, cell by cell, the build height with each aligned target and missing layer, which is a multiplicative layer-selection job. r3c3 gets layer 0 right but fails on upper layers. The cost is about 14% more compute, so about 127k steps. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.174 or the agent still places few bricks above layer 0.
last_analysis: The key problem is aligning the shifted target with the build. A full-grid circular kernel shared by all channels (r3c3, 0.174, both seeds 0.14 and 0.21) clearly beats per-channel kernels (about 0.077), the per-axis kernels (0.039) and a non-equivariant Linear (0). The main failure is collapsing to DONE early, which leaves dev success at 0. It hit 2 epochs, lr 0.002 and gamma 0.99, all with weaker or same-network aligners. Collapse looks like a race: the agent must learn rewarding placements before DONE's 0 reward wins. A faster-learning aligner wins that race. r3c3 gets layer 0 almost right but stops early, misses upper layers and does not handle overhangs. For the final round all three candidates keep the shared aligner and change one thing each: more samples (2 epochs), more per-cell capacity for comparing layers, and better credit for the exact-build bonus (longer rollouts, lambda 0.95).
